_comment: THE ART PIPELINE (yours to edit!). Each entry in 'assets' is one image the generator can produce: run `python3 tools/genart.py` from the bladesigil folder and it creates every asset whose output file doesn't exist yet (already-generated art is never touched — delete a file, or run with --force sigil_shape_blade, to redo it). 'styles' are shared style preambles: an asset's full prompt = its style text + its own 'prompt', so a whole category stays consistent and you tune the look in ONE place. Fields per asset: 'id' (for --force/--only), 'style' (a key from styles, optional), 'prompt' (the art direction — this is where you work), 'out' (game-ready file, written after post-processing), 'size' (longest edge in px for the game copy; the full-size original is always kept in assets/_originals/gen/), 'post' = 'alpha' (for sigil layers: white-art-on-black-background becomes white-with-transparency so the engine can tint it any color) or omit it for normal opaque art (monster cards, portraits). Optional 'reference': path to an existing image sent along with the prompt — 'like this, but...' consistency with art you already have. The Gemini model and your API key are read by tools/genart.py (key lives in tools/gemini_key.txt, NEVER in this file). ALL prompts below are first drafts — CONTENT FLAGS, rewrite freely!

styles.sigil_shape: A heraldic emblem for a fantasy RPG sigil system: a single bold flat symbol in PURE WHITE on a PURE BLACK background. Woodcut / coat-of-arms stencil style, thick confident silhouette with simple interior cut lines, perfectly centered, filling about 70% of a square frame. No color, no gradients, no text, no border, nothing else in the frame. The subject:
styles.sigil_bearing: A heraldic OVERLAY layer for a fantasy RPG sigil system, designed to be composited OVER a separate central emblem: PURE WHITE linework on a PURE BLACK background, woodcut style, bold and simple. CRITICAL: the CENTER of the frame must stay almost entirely black/empty so the emblem beneath shows through — this layer lives at the edges, top, or as thin lines crossing the middle. No color, no text, no central object. The overlay:
styles.monster_card: A fantasy RPG monster illustration in the style of a dark painted card: dramatic lighting, muted dungeon palette, the creature framed as a full scene with a simple dark stone background, painterly detail, no text, no border, square composition.
styles.fx_sprite: A spell-effect sprite for a fantasy RPG battle: a single glowing element in PURE WHITE on a PURE BLACK background, soft luminous edges, bold simple readable silhouette, centered, filling most of a square frame. No color, no text, no border, nothing else. The element:
styles.hero_portrait: A fantasy RPG character PORTRAIT: an EXTREME CLOSE-UP of the head and shoulders ONLY — the face fills most of the frame, cropped at the upper chest. NO waist, NO hands, NO weapons in frame. Dark painted card style: dramatic lighting, muted palette, painterly detail, simple dark background, no text, no border, square composition. The character:
styles.hero_cutout: A paperdoll cutout sprite for a fantasy RPG: ONE character, FULL BODY from the top of the head to the soles of the boots, standing in a relaxed heroic pose. The figure is ISOLATED on a plain flat PURE WHITE background — no scene, no floor, no shadow, no glow, no vignette, nothing but the figure. Painterly detail, dramatic lighting on the figure itself, no text, no border. Paint the SAME character as the reference portrait — same face, same hair, same armor. The character:
styles.prop_cutout: A dungeon-prop cutout sprite for a fantasy RPG, seen from a high three-quarter angle as if resting on a dungeon floor: ONE object, ISOLATED on a plain flat PURE WHITE background — no scene, no floor, no shadow, no glow, no text, no border, nothing but the object. Painterly detail, dramatic lighting on the object itself, a bold silhouette that stays readable at very small size. The object:
styles.dungeon_tile: A single square dungeon map tile for a fantasy RPG, in crisp 16-bit pixel-art style, seen from the same straight-on or top-down angle as the reference image when one is given. The subject fills the ENTIRE square frame edge to edge — no white mat, no border, no text, muted dungeon stone palette. The tile:
